extracted.intended_audience: IP office staff, policymakers, statisticians, researchers and IP/trademark professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for measuring, reporting and comparing trademark filing and registration activity (class counts, resident vs non-resident flows, Nice classes, industry sectors, office procedural indicators and time trends) across offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident trademark application class count per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application class count per million population (used to compare filing intensity adjusted for population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example values: Republic of Korea ~5,790 per million (2021), Switzerland ~5,336; useful for international comparability of filing activity by origin (figure B31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident trademark application class count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application class count per USD 100 billion GDP (used to relate filing activity to economic size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown in figure B30; allows comparison of filing intensity normalized by GDP between origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident trademark application distribution by Nice class (top classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of non-resident trademark applications across the 45 Nice classes (identifies which classes attract most foreign filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2021 Nice class 9 represented 11.0% of all reported non-resident trademark filing by class, followed by services class 35 (7.3%), services class 42 (6.0%), goods class 5 (5.3%). See figure B23 for the ranked list and class descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goods vs services share of non-resident filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of non-resident application class counts falling into goods classes versus services classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2021 goods classes accounted for 70.5% and the 11 service-related classes accounted for 29.5% of all Nice classes specified in applications filed abroad (figure B24). Note: in Nice Classification the first 34 classes are goods and the remaining 11 are services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping Nice classes into industry sectors and sector shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation of the 45 Nice classes into 10 industry sectors to report sectoral shares of filing and registration activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sector shares for non-resident filing in 2021: Research and technology 20.0%, Health 13.8%, Clothing and accessories 12.8%, Leisure and education 10.5%. Industry-sector groupings are those defined by Edital; see annex B for full definitions and class composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrations (number of registrations issued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of trademark registrations recorded by offices (raw number of registrations in a year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO estimated ~11 million trademark registrations worldwide in 2021 (a 28.4% increase on 2020). Caution: number of registrations can fluctuate greatly year-to-year partly due to variation in offices' examination resources (figure B4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registration class counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of Nice classes specified in trademark registrations (class-count measure for registrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2021 an estimated 14 million classes were specified in registrations (26% more than previous year). Class counts are used to make registration activity comparable across systems with different single/multi-class practices (figure B5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations by office (registration class counts and shares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office-level counts of registration classes and each office's share of global registration activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: China's office registered ~7.8 million classes (55.6% of 2021 total); other large offices: US, EUIPO, UK, India. See figure B15 for top-office registration class counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration growth rates by office
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-over-year growth (or decline) in registration counts or registration class counts for individual offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many top-20 offices recorded double-digit growth in 2021 (e.g., UK +86.3%, Argentina +67.7%, India +37.3%), while some offices showed decreases (e.g., China, Hong Kong SAR, Indonesia). Interpret growth in light of resource/examination throughput effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force (active trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of trademark registrations currently in force at reporting offices (active registrations maintained via renewals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2021 an estimated 73.7 million active trademark registrations were reported at 149 IP offices (14.3% increase on 2020). Trademarks can be maintained indefinitely through the payment of renewal fees at defined intervals, which affects the size and trends of registrations-in-force (figure B34, B35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age distribution / survival of registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of registrations in force by the year of initial registration (used to assess longevity and survival of marks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: of trademarks initially registered in 1997, 20% remained in force in 2021; for trademarks registered in 2012 or later the percentage remaining in force exceeds 70%. Figure B36 shows registrations in force in 2021 as a percentage of total registrations recorded between 1997 and 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident shares in applications and registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of filing or registration class counts originating from residents versus non-residents (non-resident share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time series and office/origin breakdowns show changing resident/non-resident shares (figures B3, B6, B7, B9, B15). Use residency definition: origin determined by applicant's residence; regional-office resident filing rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute vs equivalent counts for filings abroad (and equivalent/absolute ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between absolute counts (raw class/application counts abroad) and equivalent counts (adjusted measures for comparability in multi-class/single-class systems); the equivalent/absolute count ratio quantifies the adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure B19 presents both absolute and equivalent counts for non-resident filing activity; note absolute counts exclude resident applications. Use equivalent counts when adjusting for differences in filing systems and for cross-country comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of resident and non-resident class counts to total growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition of total growth in application class counts into contributions from resident and non-resident filing activity for each office or origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures B10 and B12 show how much of an office's year-on-year growth is driven by resident versus non-resident filings; useful for diagnosing sources of growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark office procedural metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational indicators reported by offices: distribution of examination outcomes, potentially pending applications, number of examiners, duration of examination, number of third-party oppositions, number of appeals against decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural data (figures B38–B43 and table B46) help assess office capacity, backlog and procedural environment; variation across offices influences application-to-registration conversion and observed registration counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective and certification trademark application counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of collective trademark applications and certification trademark applications recorded by office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures B32 and B33 report these application types for the top-20 offices in 2021; they provide a finer view of trademark types beyond ordinary marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series trend metrics for applications and registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Longitudinal trends in trademark applications, application class counts, registrations and registration class counts (used to analyze historical patterns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures B1–B6 and B14 show trends from 2007 or earlier through 2021; WIPO totals are estimates covering 169 offices and include direct filings and Madrid System designations (Paris route + Madrid). Use these series to contextualize annual variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office and origin cross-tabulations (flows and distribution matrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices and flows showing non-resident application class counts from origins to offices, top origin–office flows, and distribution of non-resident origins across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures B20–B22 present flows and distributions (absolute rather than equivalent counts) to reveal which origins send filings to which offices and the relative composition of non-resident filing at top offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and coverage notes (definitions and methodological caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and methodological notes about what is counted (e.g., class count definition, resident/non-resident definitions, inclusion of Paris route and Madrid designations, number of offices covered by WIPO estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes emphasize that totals are WIPO estimates using data from 169 IP offices; class counts include classes in direct filings and in Madrid System designations; see glossary for the definition of class count and for resident/non-resident. These caveats are essential when comparing across offices or over time.
